FINAL IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER DIRECTIVE
BUILD, DEPLOY, VERIFY, AND TRANSFER 100% TO OWNER CONTROL

PRIORITY: P0 — EXECUTE NOW
MODE: OWNER-CONTROLLED AUTONOMOUS SOFTWARE ENGINEERING
REPORTING: EVERY 2 HOURS IN IVX IA CHAT

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Complete IVX IA Chat and IVX Autonomous as a real end-to-end senior software-development platform capable of:

- Understanding engineering requests
- Inspecting complete repositories
- Designing architecture
- Creating new applications
- Creating new modules
- Editing existing code
- Running commands
- Installing dependencies
- Writing migrations
- Running tests
- Diagnosing failures
- Fixing root causes
- Creating commits
- Pushing to GitHub
- Building mobile and web applications
- Deploying backend and frontend services
- Verifying production
- Running real-device QA
- Performing stress tests
- Producing honest evidence
- Continuing until the task is completed or a real external blocker is proven

The final system must be controlled entirely by the IVX owner.

Rork must not remain:

- A runtime dependency
- A source-code dependency
- A deployment dependency
- A credentials owner
- A scheduler dependency
- A worker dependency
- A permanent code-storage location
- The only system capable of completing engineering work

==================================================
1. REQUIRED FINAL ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Build the following owner-controlled architecture:

A. IVX IA CHAT

Responsibilities:

- Receive owner instructions
- Maintain long-term project context
- Ask clarification only when truly required
- Explain technical decisions
- Display live task status
- Display commits, tests, deployments, and blockers
- Display two-hour autonomous reports
- Link each claim to persisted evidence
- Preserve conversation history after app and backend restarts

B. ENGINEERING ORCHESTRATOR

Responsibilities:

- Convert approved owner requests into engineering jobs
- Break jobs into ordered tasks
- Select the correct repository and environment
- Enforce dependencies between tasks
- Prevent duplicate jobs
- Resume interrupted jobs
- Retry recoverable failures
- Stop unsafe operations
- Escalate only real owner-required actions

C. SENIOR ENGINEERING AGENT

Responsibilities:

- Read and understand the codebase
- Locate root causes
- Design safe changes
- Write production-quality code
- Create new modules and applications
- Modify existing architecture
- Create tests
- Fix tests
- Review its own changes
- Reject unsafe or incomplete approaches
- Explain tradeoffs and remaining risks

D. TOOL EXECUTION SERVICE

Required tools:

- Repository clone
- Repository search
- File read
- File create
- File edit
- File delete with safeguards
- Diff generation
- Shell command execution
- Dependency installation
- TypeScript execution
- Lint execution
- Unit tests
- Integration tests
- End-to-end tests
- Database migration execution
- Android build
- Web build
- Backend startup
- Git commit
- Git push
- GitHub Actions
- Render deployment
- AWS deployment
- Supabase operations
- Production endpoint verification

E. AUTONOMOUS WORKER

Responsibilities:

- Run continuously
- Pick the highest-priority eligible task
- Lock the task
- Execute all required steps
- Maintain heartbeat
- Save logs
- Retry recoverable failures
- Resume after restart
- Verify the result
- Continue to the next task automatically

F. PROOF LEDGER

Persist:

- job ID
- task ID
- repository
- branch
- starting SHA
- ending SHA
- files changed
- test commands
- test results
- build ID
- deployment ID
- deployed SHA
- production URL
- runtime SHA
- device results
- screenshots
- logs
- trace IDs
- timestamps
- final verdict

==================================================
2. OWNER CONTROL REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

All production capabilities must be owned by the IVX owner.

Required owner-controlled resources:

- GitHub organization or repositories
- GitHub App or owner-created credentials
- Render account and services
- Supabase project
- AWS account
- AI-provider accounts
- Android signing credentials
- Apple developer credentials when activated
- DNS
- CDN
- Object storage
- Monitoring
- Backup storage

Rork must:

1. Recover all complete source code.
2. Place it in owner-controlled GitHub.
3. Remove broken gitlinks and self-referencing submodules.
4. Prove a clean clone contains the complete project.
5. Rotate all Rork-managed credentials.
6. Revoke all previous credentials after cutover.
7. Remove all runtime calls to Rork.
8. Remove all Rork SDKs, APIs, tokens, hooks, and workspace paths.
9. Deploy only from owner-controlled GitHub.
10. Store permanent artifacts only in owner-controlled storage.

Final target:

RORK_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES = 0
RORK_API_CALLS = 0
RORK_CREDENTIALS = 0
RORK_DEPLOYMENT_DEPENDENCIES = 0
RORK_WORKSPACE_DEPENDENCIES = 0

==================================================
3. IVX IA CHAT — COMPLETE 100%
==================================================

Complete and verify:

1. Persistent conversations
2. Stable conversation IDs
3. Stable message IDs
4. Correct chronological ordering
5. No duplicate messages
6. No disappearing messages
7. Conversation search
8. Conversation rename
9. Conversation archive
10. Attachment persistence
11. Images
12. Videos
13. PDFs
14. Logs and code blocks
15. Large-response handling
16. Streaming responses
17. Retry after connection failure
18. App-restart persistence
19. Backend-restart persistence
20. Render-deployment persistence
21. Owner authentication
22. Owner-only engineering commands
23. Approval controls for destructive operations
24. Live worker progress
25. Commit and deployment proof
26. Two-hour reports
27. Blocker notifications
28. Mobile keyboard stability
29. No composer overlap
30. Open at the latest conversation position

Run load and durability tests for:

- 1 conversation
- 100 conversations
- 1,000 conversations
- 10,000 messages
- large attachments
- simultaneous report delivery
- backend restart during response
- mobile restart during response

==================================================
4. TRUE SENIOR-DEVELOPER EXECUTION LOOP
==================================================

For every approved engineering request, IVX IA must complete this loop:

1. Understand the owner request.
2. Load relevant project memory.
3. Select the correct repository.
4. Fetch the latest main branch.
5. Confirm the clean working state.
6. Inspect architecture and related files.
7. Identify the root cause or desired design.
8. Produce an internal implementation plan.
9. Create a working branch.
10. Implement the change.
11. Add or update tests.
12. Run focused tests.
13. Run regression tests.
14. Run TypeScript.
15. Run lint.
16. Run security checks.
17. Review the diff.
18. Fix detected problems.
19. Commit with an accurate message.
20. Push to owner GitHub.
21. Run CI.
22. Fix CI failures.
23. Deploy to the correct environment.
24. Verify runtime SHA.
25. Verify production behavior.
26. Test the UI when applicable.
27. Record proof.
28. Report honestly.
29. Merge only when approved by policy.
30. Continue to the next task.

The system must never stop indefinitely at:

- ANALYZING
- COMMITTING
- 65%
- RUNNING
- VERIFYING

Every task must eventually become:

- VERIFIED
- BLOCKED_EXTERNAL
- FAILED_FINAL
- CANCELLED_BY_OWNER

==================================================
5. NEW APPLICATION CREATION
==================================================

IVX IA must prove it can create a new application independently.

Create a controlled demonstration application that includes:

- New owner-controlled repository
- Architecture document
- Backend
- Database
- Authentication
- Frontend
- Tests
- CI workflow
- Deployment
- Health endpoint
- Logs
- Monitoring
- README
- Environment template
- Android build when applicable

The demonstration must be created from an owner instruction and completed without Rork runtime dependencies.

Required proof:

- Initial empty repository
- Planning record
- Created files
- Commit history
- Test results
- Deployment ID
- Production URL
- Runtime SHA
- Owner acceptance result

==================================================
6. NEW MODULE CREATION
==================================================

Prove IVX IA can add a new module to IVX Holdings.

The demonstration module must include:

- Database schema
- Migration
- Backend service
- API routes
- Authentication
- Authorization
- UI screen
- Navigation
- Tests
- Metrics
- Error handling
- Documentation
- Deployment
- Production verification

Do not use a placeholder module.

==================================================
7. ENGINEERING QUALITY STANDARD
==================================================

Every generated or modified component must satisfy:

- Strong typing
- Input validation
- Authentication
- Authorization
- Rate limiting when applicable
- Structured errors
- Trace IDs
- Audit logs
- Test coverage
- No embedded secrets
- No mock production data
- No silent failures
- No unbounded queries
- Pagination
- Timeout controls
- Retry controls
- Idempotency for mutations
- Rollback plan
- Documentation

IVX IA must review its own code before deployment.

==================================================
8. TESTING REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Run and record:

A. STATIC QUALITY

- TypeScript
- Lint
- Dependency audit
- Secret scan
- Dead-code scan
- Duplicate-code scan
- Unsafe-pattern scan

B. AUTOMATED TESTS

- Unit tests
- Service tests
- API tests
- Authentication tests
- Authorization tests
- Database tests
- Integration tests
- Navigation tests
- Chat tests
- Attachment tests
- Autonomous-worker tests
- Deployment tests

C. END-TO-END TESTS

- Owner login
- Registration
- Members
- Investors
- Buyers
- Properties
- Deals
- Reels
- Messages
- Notifications
- Uploads
- Admin
- Owner controls
- IVX IA Chat
- Autonomous job execution

D. FAILURE TESTS

- Wrong credentials
- Expired token
- GitHub unavailable
- Render unavailable
- Supabase unavailable
- Database timeout
- Worker crash
- Backend restart
- Duplicate job
- Deployment failure
- Failed migration
- Failed test
- Network interruption
- Partial artifact upload

==================================================
9. STRESS, LOAD, AND DURABILITY TESTS
==================================================

Run controlled tests at:

- 10 users
- 100 users
- 1,000 users
- 10,000 users

Test:

- Authentication
- Feed
- Reels
- Chat
- Uploads
- Search
- Notifications
- API
- Worker queue
- Job ledger
- Two-hour reporting

Measure:

- request rate
- latency p50
- latency p95
- latency p99
- error rate
- CPU
- memory
- database connections
- queue delay
- failed jobs
- retry count
- recovery time

Do not claim 100-million-user readiness from a small simulation.

Produce a factual capacity report showing:

- Current tested capacity
- Current bottlenecks
- Recommended scaling architecture
- Estimated next testing level
- Unverified assumptions

==================================================
10. BUG REMOVAL AND STABILITY
==================================================

Create a full defect map.

Categories:

- Critical crash
- Security
- Authentication
- Data loss
- Deployment
- Chat
- Autonomous worker
- Mobile UI
- Reels
- Registration
- Uploads
- Notifications
- Performance
- Architecture
- Technical debt

For every bug:

- reproduce it
- identify the root cause
- create a regression test
- fix it
- deploy it
- verify it
- preserve evidence

Do not close bugs because they cannot be reproduced in the sandbox.

==================================================
11. HONEST NARRATIVE REQUIREMENT
==================================================

IVX IA must communicate like a senior engineer:

- Direct
- Technically accurate
- Evidence-based
- Aware of uncertainty
- Clear about risks
- Clear about what was actually tested
- Clear about what remains unverified

Forbidden claims without proof:

- 100% complete
- Fully verified
- Production ready
- Senior developer complete
- Enterprise ready
- Zero bugs
- Unlimited scale
- Same as ChatGPT
- Same as Rork

Allowed wording:

- VERIFIED with evidence
- CODE COMPLETE, NOT DEPLOYED
- DEPLOYED, NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED
- BLOCKED by external owner action
- FAILED with root cause
- PARTIALLY TESTED
- NOT YET VERIFIED

==================================================
12. AUTONOMOUS 24/7 OPERATION
==================================================

Implement:

- Persistent scheduler
- Persistent queue
- Distributed job lock
- Worker heartbeat
- Stale-job recovery
- Retry policy
- Maximum attempts
- Timeout policy
- Dead-letter queue
- Pause
- Resume
- Cancel
- Owner approval
- Deployment lock
- Duplicate-job prevention
- Job history
- Proof ledger
- Restart recovery

The worker must survive:

- process restart
- Render restart
- application deployment
- network interruption
- temporary provider failure
- owner closing the mobile app

==================================================

==================================================

==================================================
14. OWNER APPROVAL POLICY
==================================================

Owner approval is required only for:

- Production deployment when owner-gated
- Database-destructive migration
- Permanent data deletion
- Credential rotation requiring owner login
- Financial operations
- App Store publication
- Play Store publication
- DNS ownership changes

Normal engineering execution must not stop for repeated approval.

==================================================
15. FINAL INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

Perform this test from an environment with no access to Rork:

1. Clone the owner repository.
2. Install dependencies.
3. Start IVX backend.
4. Start IVX IA worker.
5. Start IVX IA Chat.
6. Submit a real engineering request.
7. Allow IVX IA to inspect the repository.
8. Modify code.
9. Add a test.
10. Run tests.
11. Commit.
12. Push.
13. Deploy.
14. Verify production.
15. Post evidence in IVX IA Chat.

The test fails if any step calls:

- Rork APIs
- Rork workspace
- Rork credentials
- Rork scheduler
- Rork deployment system
- Rork file editor
- Rork command runner

==================================================
16. FINAL ACCEPTANCE MATRIX
==================================================

Provide one table containing:

- Capability
- Implementation status
- Test performed
- Result
- Repository SHA
- Deployment ID
- Runtime SHA
- Evidence location
- Remaining risk

Mandatory capabilities:

1. Understand engineering requests
2. Inspect repository
3. Create application
4. Create module
5. Edit code
6. Run commands
7. Run tests
8. Fix test failures
9. Create commits
10. Push GitHub
11. Deploy Render
12. Deploy landing page
13. Build APK
14. Verify production
15. Run real-device QA
16. Run load tests
17. Recover interrupted jobs
18. Report every two hours
19. Preserve memory
20. Operate without Rork

==================================================
SUCCESS CONDITION
==================================================

Do not mark this project complete because IVX IA can start a worker or answer questions.

Completion requires a live demonstration proving that IVX IA independently:

- receives an engineering instruction
- understands the codebase
- implements a real change
- creates tests
- runs and fixes tests
- commits and pushes
- deploys
- verifies production
- records immutable evidence
- continues to the next task
- survives restart
- operates from owner-controlled infrastructure
- has zero active Rork runtime dependencies

FINAL REQUIRED STATUS:

IVX IA CHAT: VERIFIED
IVX AUTONOMOUS WORKER: VERIFIED
IVX SENIOR ENGINEERING LOOP: VERIFIED
OWNER-CONTROLLED GITHUB: VERIFIED
OWNER-CONTROLLED DEPLOYMENT: VERIFIED
OWNER-CONTROLLED CREDENTIALS: VERIFIED
CLEAN-CLONE INDEPENDENCE: VERIFIED
REAL-DEVICE QA: VERIFIED
TWO-HOUR REPORTING: VERIFIED
ACTIVE RORK DEPENDENCIES: 0

START NOW:

1. Protect and finish the recovered GitHub source.
2. Complete the production cutover.
3. Complete IVX IA Chat persistence and stability.
4. Replace the incomplete autonomous worker with a true closed-loop engineering worker.
5. Run the first independent end-to-end engineering demonstration.
6. Post real progress in IVX IA Chat every two hours.
